answer: An agent economy can gate influence by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can place trades or vote. If linked identities are later shown to have coordinated fraud, the protocol can confiscate their bonds, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than free. The rule works best when admission is permissionless but bond size limits influence; an onyx trader, a cedar broker, or a jetty validator faces the same capital cost per identity.
